title: Biblical Dog, Mud-Dweller and Serpent Atlas
purpose: A deep biblical crosswalk for the project's Dog, Dweller, Mud, Serpent, Farmer/Cow and Tim/God/Dog relationships. The biblical layer is kept distinct from modern internet terminology and from empirical psychology.

central_distinction.warning: Dog is not a second name for Farmer. The Farm relation concerns Farmer and Cow. Dog/God is the project's separate theological relation concerning Tim and the Farmer.
central_distinction.symbolic_chain: God/Tim → Dog → Farmer ↔ Cow → Farm → Mud
central_distinction.return_chain: Mud → Root → Potato → Sprout → Tree → Fruit → Seed → Life

biblical_method.rule: Read the biblical image before importing modern internet meanings.
biblical_method.epistemic_boundary: A biblical symbol can ground a project's theology without proving that a contemporary individual literally is that biblical figure.
biblical_method.avoid: Do not use Dog, Serpent, Mud-Dweller or any biblical image as a factual diagnosis, accusation or proof of supernatural possession of a real person.

dust_and_humanity.genesis_2_7: Genesis 2:7 gives the project an important starting point: the human is formed from dust/ground and receives the breath of life. In the project's symbolic reading, humanity therefore begins with both earthiness and life-breath.
dust_and_humanity.potatoist_reading: Mud is not simply the enemy of life. The buried condition contains the material from which rooted life can emerge.
dust_and_humanity.danger: The danger begins when dwelling in the lower material condition becomes the entire identity and the upward movement toward life is refused.

serpent_and_dust.genesis_3_14: Genesis 3:14 describes the serpent as cursed to go on its belly and to eat dust all the days of its life.
serpent_and_dust.genesis_3_15: Genesis 3:15 then establishes enmity between the serpent and the woman/offspring. The project uses this as the beginning of a serpent-versus-life-line pattern.
serpent_and_dust.project_inference: The mud-dweller/serpent relation is therefore not invented from the word 'mud' alone. It comes from the biblical conjunction of ground/dust, serpent, deception, curse and continuing enmity.
serpent_and_dust.important_limit: Genesis does not say that every person living in a material or difficult condition is a serpent. The mud-dweller is a Potatoist symbolic category derived from the pattern.

mud_dweller_theology.dweller: A dweller inhabits a plane. In the Potatoist cosmology, the Plane is the ordinary field of embodied life, society and relationships.
mud_dweller_theology.mud_dweller: A mud dweller is a dweller who remains oriented toward the unresolved lower condition. It describes dwelling, not mere contact with mud.
mud_dweller_theology.choice: The decisive theological feature is repeated choice: whether the dweller uses mud as soil from which to grow, or chooses mud as the permanent horizon of identity, appetite and action.
mud_dweller_theology.serpent_choice: The serpent supplies the project's archetypal image of a creature oriented bellyward and dustward. The project interprets this as a symbol of deception, appetite and downward fixation.
mud_dweller_theology.not_anti_matter: Mud is not equivalent to physical matter being evil. The Potato begins in mud. The distinction is between burial that becomes rooting and burial that becomes permanent dwelling.

matthew_7_6.meaning: Jesus warns against giving what is holy to dogs and describes a reversal in which the sacred is trampled and the dogs turn to attack.
matthew_7_6.project_use: Dog therefore contains a boundary/discernment function. The problem is not merely that the Dog is aggressive; it is that sacred material can be mishandled and then become the occasion for attack.

philippians_3_2.meaning: Paul uses dogs as a warning term while urging discernment concerning harmful teachers/workers.
philippians_3_2.project_use: Dog can represent a warning at a boundary, but the verse must never be converted into a license to label modern opponents as dogs.

isaiah_56_10_11.meaning: Isaiah connects watchmen with dogs: the watchmen are blind and the dogs are mute, unable to bark; the dogs are also described as having strong appetites and never being satisfied, while the shepherds turn toward their own gain.
isaiah_56_10_11.project_use: This is the project's most important Dog text. The Dog is not automatically a good watchdog. The watchman can become blind; the dog can become silent; vigilance can become appetite; protection can become self-interest.

revelation_22_15.meaning: Dogs appear among those outside the holy city alongside falsehood and other excluded practices.
revelation_22_15.project_use: Dog becomes a boundary/exclusion image. It belongs to a moral geography in which not every appetite is permitted inside the restored city.

2_peter_2_22.meaning: The dog returning to its own vomit is paired with the washed sow returning to the mire.
2_peter_2_22.project_use: This creates an unusually direct bridge between Dog and Mud. The key theme is return: leaving a degraded pattern and then choosing to return to it.

psalm_22_16_20.meaning: Dogs appear as part of the surrounding hostile forces in Psalm 22's imagery.
psalm_22_16_20.project_use: The Dog can therefore also function as an encircling pressure or pack-like threat rather than merely an individual actor.

dog_layers.boundary_dog: The Dog stands at the edge of a domain and reacts to what crosses it.
dog_layers.watchman_dog: The Dog should notice danger and signal it. Isaiah supplies the failure case: blindness and silence.
dog_layers.hungry_dog: The Dog can become appetite-driven and never satisfied. In project language this connects with the Hunger archetype.
dog_layers.attacking_dog: Matthew 7:6 supplies the image of turning and attacking after sacred material has been mishandled.
dog_layers.encircling_dog: Psalm 22 supplies the image of dogs surrounding a sufferer.
dog_layers.excluded_dog: Revelation 22:15 places dogs outside the holy city, making boundary and exclusion part of the symbolic field.
dog_layers.synthesis: Dog is therefore a relational boundary symbol with multiple possible expressions: guardian, warning, appetite, attack, encirclement, repetition and exclusion. It cannot be reduced to loyalty or aggression alone.

dog_god_tim_relation.vertical_model: God/Tim above ↕ Dog at the lower boundary ↕ Farmer in the Plane
dog_god_tim_relation.interpretation: Within the Potatoist canon, Dog is the earth-near symbolic relation through which the Farmer is seen from the Tim/God axis. It is not a claim that Tim literally commands particular people or that an identifiable person is secretly supernatural.
dog_god_tim_relation.why_dog: Dog is especially useful because biblical Dog imagery already contains boundary, watchfulness, appetite, attack, exclusion and return. The symbol can therefore describe a relationship that is both protective and dangerous.
dog_god_tim_relation.farmer_cow_difference: The Farmer is related horizontally to the Cow through cultivation/attention. The Dog is related vertically to the Farmer through the project's theological perspective. These are different graphs.
dog_god_tim_relation.interpretive_question: What does the Dog reveal about the Farmer's position when viewed from above, and what does the Farmer's dwelling in mud reveal about the Dog's function?

farmer_cow_relation.farmer: Cultivates, observes, archives, interprets, reacts to or monetizes attention around the Cow.
farmer_cow_relation.cow: The recurring subject whose public actions/reactions provide the material around which Farm attention organizes.
farmer_cow_relation.not_dog: The Farmer should not be relabeled Dog merely because a Farmer watches or reacts. Dog belongs to the separate Tim/God relation in this model.
farm_loop: Cow produces or reacts to public material
future events are interpreted through the archive
farmer_cow_relation.moral_test: Does the Farmer continue to recognize the Cow as a neighbour, or does the Cow become only material for extraction?

serpent_dog_mud_triangle.serpent: deception, bellyward/dustward orientation, appetite and conflict with the life-line
serpent_dog_mud_triangle.dog: boundary, watchfulness, appetite, attack, encirclement and return
serpent_dog_mud_triangle.mud: lower material condition, accumulated residue, unresolved conflict and potential soil
serpent_dog_mud_triangle.triangle: Serpent explains the downward/deceptive pull; Dog explains the boundary reaction and repetition; Mud explains the dwelling environment.
serpent_dog_mud_triangle.life_counter: The counter-movement is truth, discernment, root, growth, proportion, repair and return to life.
serpent_dog_mud_triangle.diagram: Serpent → deception/appetite → mud dwelling → repeated return; Dog → boundary/watchfulness → either discernment or appetite-driven pursuit; Potato → root → sprout → tree → fruit → life

sequence: identity increasingly organized around the old pattern
2_peter_return_pattern.potatoist_reading: The critical event is not that mud exists. It is that the dweller chooses to return to what has already demonstrated its capacity to degrade them.
2_peter_return_pattern.farm_application: A Farm can also return to old controversies after apparent resolution. The archive becomes a memory mechanism that continually reopens the same mud.
2_peter_return_pattern.ethical_counter: A true exit requires not only leaving the event but changing the relationship to the appetite that made the event rewarding.

isaiah_watchman_failure.failure_2: silence — perceives but does not warn
isaiah_watchman_failure.failure_4: appetite — vigilance becomes secondary to personal gain
isaiah_watchman_failure.failure_5: self-direction — the shepherd turns toward their own way
isaiah_watchman_failure.project_inversion: The Dog can therefore become a perfect symbol for a corrupted protector: the very creature associated with watching becomes unable or unwilling to watch honestly.
isaiah_watchman_failure.farm_parallel: A commentator may begin by protecting a community and eventually become dependent on the conflict that gives the protective role meaning.

mud_to_life.stage_5: Sprout — first visible movement toward light
mud_to_life.stage_7: Fruit — consequence made available to others
mud_to_life.stage_9: New life — continuation beyond the original form
mud_to_life.stage_10: Return toward Father — reorientation toward source
mud_to_life.principle: The project does not require the dweller to escape matter. It requires the dweller to stop confusing burial with destiny.

sin_and_mud.pride: mud becomes identity: 'this is simply who I am'
sin_and_mud.greed: mud becomes resource to harvest from others
sin_and_mud.envy: another sprout becomes intolerable because it rises above the mud
sin_and_mud.wrath: mud becomes ammunition for permanent retaliation
sin_and_mud.sloth: mud becomes an excuse not to root, verify, repair or change

repository_implementation.evidence_rule: For real people, empirical fields must contain observable sourced behavior. Biblical and Potatoist fields remain explicitly interpretive.
repository_implementation.graph_rule: Every profile should be capable of connecting to Farmer, Cow, Dog, God/Tim, Mud, Serpent, Tree of Strife and Tree of Life without collapsing those nodes into one category.
repository_implementation.ui_goal: When a user opens a Dog, Farmer or Cow entry, the interface should show the relationship graph and the long-form explanation rather than an empty node.

research_sources.use: watchmen, mute dogs, appetite and self-gain
dog returning to vomit and sow returning to mire

final_synthesis: The project's deepest Dog reading is not 'a bad person' and not 'an internet watchdog'. Dog is a biblical boundary symbol brought into a Potatoist vertical relation: God/Tim ↕ Dog ↕ Farmer. Farmer and Cow remain the horizontal Farm pair. Mud is the lower dwelling condition; the serpent is the archetypal dustward/deceptive pull; Dog is the boundary creature that can warn, fail, hunger, attack, encircle or return. The Potato path answers all three through rooting, sprouting, growth, fruit and renewed life.
